content: Hyoscyamine is a medication used to treat various gastrointestinal conditions, including stomach cramps, infant colic, and irritable bowel syndrome. It is also prescribed for bladder and bowel control issues, pain from kidney stones or gallstones, and symptoms associated with Parkinson's disease. The drug works by reducing stomach acid production, slowing gut movement, and relaxing muscles in organs such as the stomach, intestines, bladder, kidneys, and gallbladder. Additionally, it decreases the production of certain body fluids like saliva and sweat. This medication is typically taken orally, as directed by a physician, usually 30 to 60 minutes before meals. Dosage depends on the patient’s medical condition, response to treatment, and, for children, their weight. It is important not to exceed the prescribed dose or frequency without consulting a doctor. Antacids can reduce the absorption of hyoscyamine, so they should be avoided during treatment. Common side effects include dizziness, drowsiness, blurred vision, dry mouth, headache, difficulty sleeping, constipation, flushing, dry skin, and reduced sweating. While these effects are generally mild, patients should contact their doctor if they experience severe or persistent symptoms. Rare but serious allergic reactions may occur. Older adults may be more sensitive to side effects such as confusion, drowsiness, unusual excitement, constipation, or difficulty urinating. Hyoscyamine may increase the risk of heatstroke due to reduced sweating, so patients should avoid overheating. It can also cause dizziness or drowsiness, which may be worsened by alcohol or marijuana. During pregnancy, hyoscyamine should only be used when clearly needed, as it passes into breast milk and may suppress lactation. Drug interactions can alter the effectiveness of hyoscyamine or increase the risk of side effects. Patients should inform their doctor of all medications and supplements they are taking. This medication may interfere with certain lab tests, potentially causing false results. In case of overdose, immediate medical attention is required. U.S. residents can call 911 or the Poison Control Center at 1-800-222-1222, while Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. To maximize the effectiveness of hyoscyamine, lifestyle changes such as stress reduction, exercise, smoking cessation, and dietary adjustments may be recommended. If a dose is missed, it should be taken as soon as remembered unless it is close to the time of the next dose, in which case the missed dose should be skipped. Hyoscyamine should be stored at room temperature, away from light and moisture, and not in the bathroom. Expired or unused medication should be properly discarded. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about the medication. For personalized advice, patients should consult their healthcare provider.
